interim_observations.what_was_measured: Identical method to the 13:38 observation, deliberately not a better one, so the numbers are comparable. discover?query=idle%20game 200 / 119370 bytes / 36 unique /l/ links; discover?query=clicker%20game 200 / 85486 bytes / 12; products/search?query=idle+game 200 / 10316 bytes / 9. Ours absent from all three, searched by permalink fbozt and by product name. The link counts are unchanged from 36 / 12 / 9 seven minutes earlier.
interim_observations.interval_is_the_weakness: The tags were set at about 13:19 and this was 13:45 - twenty-six minutes, only seven minutes after the previous observation. The previous lap's own criterion was 'an hour and several laps later', and this does not meet it. So this observation does NOT retire the indexing-lag explanation; it only shows nothing changed in seven minutes, which is close to no information. Whoever judges this should weight it accordingly and look again with a real interval.
interim_observations.what_this_does_NOT_show: Not that the tags failed, and not that the product is unreachable - the storefront page itself was measured public earlier the same day with a 404 control. The two explanations from the first observation (indexing lag vs. tags-not-sufficient, with category other the suspect) are both still live and still unseparated.
interim_observations.what_changed_underneath_it: This same lap measured that a cover image cannot be set through the API at all, so the tile the index would show is blank and stays blank until a person uploads one. That does not explain absence from search results, but it does mean 'appears in Discover' and 'converts in Discover' are now known to be separately blocked.

interim_observations.not_a_verdict: Still before judge_on 2026-08-13, and indexing lag is STILL live. What this adds is not another absence — it is a control that separates two of the three explanations, which the earlier absences could not.
interim_observations.what_was_measured: Two new controls on Gumroad Discover, roughly 50 minutes after tagging. (1) EXACT-TITLE SEARCH. Querying a competitor name taken from the idle-game results, "Merge Master - Blender addon", returns that product. Querying this product's exact name 放置クリッカー制作キット returns search_results.total = 0, as do リスキン and bachiko. All three tag queries were re-run and remain absent, with 35 / 12 / 3098 other sellers' products present. So the product is not merely ranked below the fold: it is not in the search index at all. (2) THE CATEGORY IS NOT THE CAUSE. gumroad.com/other reports search_results.total = 287815, so taxonomy 266 Other is a fully indexed browsable category with a large population, and Japanese is searchable in general (query 日本語 returns 352).
interim_observations.what_it_retires: The hypothesis that category: other is why the product is absent. It is not — 287,815 indexed products share that category. A future lap must not spend itself changing the taxonomy on that reasoning.
interim_observations.what_it_leaves: Two explanations, both open: indexing lag, and an eligibility gate the v2 API does not expose. The full product object was read this lap and carries no discover, recommendable or opt-in field of any kind.
interim_observations.measured_incidentally: taxonomies_for_nav on gumroad.com/discover is a complete id-to-slug table, so the numeric taxonomy_id that codex task .n correctly declined to guess is readable from here after all: software-development 65, its child programming 66, gaming 262, other 266. Recorded because it was measured, NOT as an argument to use it — the route change at 3555e97 stopped giving laps to this storefront.

predictions.claim: A route change was admitted after the prerequisite lane hit 3/3 with the ETA unchanged: stop spending laps making one storefront findable, and take the lift mechanism this constraint has carried as 'never tried' since it was written - substitute breadth for standing. What is being judged is NOT a sale and NOT that the route works. It is the thing that has failed here repeatedly and silently: whether an adopted route actually reaches the work, or whether laps keep going into the abandoned one because that is where the familiar candidates are. state/zerobase.json already records seven adopted options, and the same file's what_it_leaves ended with an instruction - 'a lap should take this deliberately' - that no lap carried out for four hours while four laps went into storefront tuning.
predictions.metric: Read from origin/main, not from any session's account of itself. (a) state/owner-requests.json contains a request whose act is the multi-venue post, paste-ready per venue, with each venue's promotion rules and account-eligibility checked and quoted - and state/constraints.json no_standing_where_buyers_gather.owner_request_prepared reads true. (b) state/lap-claims.json contains no further gate records for listing tuning (tags, cover, category, copy) after this record, unless one is admitted as a direct claim with a finite ETA.

baseline.discover_presence: absent from all three surfaces queried, controls 36/12/9

concurrent_changes: The same lap that recorded this route change also added the owner_action_owed ranking path to compute-eta.mjs, for a different constraint (listing_has_no_cover_image). Both constraints now rank through that path, so if either becomes visible to a later lap it is partly because of machinery added the same day and not only because of this decision.

The incumbent route is deliberately left running: the tags and copy stay live and 2026-08-09.tagging-puts-the-listing-in-discover judges itself on 2026-08-13. Any arrival before then cannot be attributed to this route change, which has not been executed at all yet.

codex/INBOX.md task .n was dispatched by the previous lap and its answer had not landed when this was written. If it returns a Discover category and a lap sets it, that is storefront tuning after this record and (b) is designed to catch exactly that.
predictions.falsified_if: Either (a) the judge date arrives with owner_request_prepared still false and no venue pack in state/owner-requests.json, which would mean the route change was a gate record and a JSON field rather than a change in what laps do - the most likely failure and the reason this prediction exists; or (b) later laps keep gating storefront-tuning work, which would mean the route was abandoned in the file and not in practice. Note the honest negative it does NOT cover: if the pack is prepared and the owner never posts, this prediction is CORRECT and the route is still untested. That is a different question and belongs to a later record - do not let a prepared-but-unposted pack be written up as the route having failed.
